items.title: Pokémon TCG Reportedly Launching First-Ever Valentine’s Day Set in 2027
items.description: Pokémon TCG is reportedly launching its first-ever Valentine's Day box set on January 27, 2027, featuring mini packs and packaging that folds into a classroom mailbox.
items.author: Sara Heritage
items.content:
The Pokémon Company is intending to launch the franchise's very first dedicated Valentine's Day collection on January 27, 2027, according to a recent report from Pokébeach.

While the Valentine set is yet to be officially confirmed, the leaks reportedly suggest that the "Pokémon TCG Valentine’s Box" will be similar in practice to the popular Trick or Trade Halloween series, rather than a full expansion release like Pokémon TCG's Delta Reign or Chaos Rising expansions.

These seasonal sets typically come in compact foil packs containing three cards, alongside sticker sheets. The Halloween releases were given their own pumpkin-stamped Pikachu, so I'd put good money on the Valentine's version getting some kind of suitably pink Pika stamp.

The Trick or Trade range was originally designed as a way for kids to hand out Pokémon cards while trick-or-treating, effectively giving them a Pokémon-themed alternative to candy. Given how expensive some Halloween sweets have become, perhaps the cards aren't such a bad substitute.

The reported Valentine's Box appears to be taking a similar approach, with the packaging and packs seemingly designed around giving cards to friends or handing them out in the classroom. The box is also apparently designed to fold into a little cardboard mailbox, allowing cards to be handed out to classmates in the same way kids might exchange Valentine's cards at school.

That's a cute idea, although given the current state of the Pokémon TCG market, I'm not entirely convinced every box will make it into the hands of an actual child.

Previous seasonal releases have generally focused on reprinted cards rather than introducing a bunch of new full-art cards, but that hasn't stopped sealed products from holding surprisingly strong secondary-market value. The Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle (last seen in 2025), for example, contains 40 mini packs with three cards apiece, and currently has a market value of around $75.99 at TCGplayer.

That makes the potential Valentine's release one to keep an eye on, particularly if it proves to be another limited seasonal product. Previous holiday releases have sold out well ahead of launch, so the real competition could come when preorders eventually open.

There's also currently no word on which Pokémon will take centre stage in the mini set. My vote would be Enamorus, although Fairy-type Pokémon aren't currently part of the TCG's standard format... Yet.

I’d also love to see Sylveon - its pink color scheme and cute ribbons would be perfect. Plus, it evolves by friendship! Other options could be Audino and Blissey, since both are linked with care and kindness - qualities that suit Valentine's Day well- or even Pikachu in loveheart-themed clothing might also show up.

Sylveon would also be an obvious choice. Its pink colour scheme and ribbons are practically made for Valentine's Day, while the fact that it evolves through friendship feels particularly appropriate. Audino and Blissey could also fit the theme nicely given their associations with care and kindness, while a loveheart-themed Pikachu would hardly come as a surprise.

items.title: Blizzard Adds Beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' Quest to World of Warcraft: Forever
items.description: For as much as World of Warcraft Forever has been making an effort to preserve the vanilla WoW experience, there are just some things in the game's history that must be added, and the quest 'Kyle's Gone Missing!' is one of them. And Blizzard just added it to Forever.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
For as much as World of Warcraft Forever has been making an effort to preserve the vanilla WoW experience, there are just some things in the game's history that must be added, and the quest 'Kyle's Gone Missing!' is one of them. And Blizzard just added it to Forever.

'Kyle's Gone Missing!' was added during the Burning Crusade expansion through a Make-a-Wish campaign in 2007 for Ezra Chatterton, who was diagnosed with brain cancer earlier that year. Chatterton, who went by the in-game name of Ephoenix, voiced the quest-giver, Ahab Wheathoof, and had his dog Kyle added to the game, which players were then tasked with finding. The quest went live in patch 2.1.2 on June 19, 2007, and has been in the game ever since.

Sadly, a little over a year later, in October 2008, Chatterton passed away at the age of 12. The quest has remained a beloved part of the game ever since, and Chatterton has also been referenced multiple times, with Blizzard re-naming the Elder of Thunderbluff (who shows up during the annual Lunar Festival) after him in Wrath of the Lich King.

But because the quest was added during The Burning Crusade, it's not part of the original game, which meant it wouldn't be in World of Warcraft Forever – even if the zone where the quest takes place is the Tauren starting zone. But, after players asked Blizzard to bring the quest to Forever, it's officially been added.

Blizzard added the patch after players asked for it in the forums, when user Nyaria posted saying, "My Husband was very sad that the Make a Wish Quest involving Kyle wasn’t in Mulgore." They even acknowledged that it doesn't fit the 'Vanilla-only' ethos, but stood by it, saying, "Yes it wasn’t added until TBC, but this is WoW: Forever, we already have new quests added in, and it was a cute little quest, and a Make a Wish addition for a poor kid."

Luckily, shortly after that thread was posted Blizzard community manager Kaivax simply posted: "We're working on it. Stay tuned." The entire rest of the thread is full of players thanking Kaivax and the rest of the Forever team for adding the quest. One player, Ikory, claimed to have been a Make-a-Wish kid who survived and thanked Blizzard in a long post, which they signed off with: "I spent 30 years in crippling pain, with a failing heart, that had to be repaired every few years. I am a survivor. I was that kid who was supposed to die. Now I have a freaken PhD. I lived. Make-A-Wish helped me have hope as a kid. I got my wish. I’m glad Ezra got his wish. Thank you Blizzard for still caring about us Make-A-Wish kids after all these years."

Now, just four days later, the quest is officially live in the World of Warcraft beta, as a part of the October 1 patch.

Johnny Cash, the Blizzard Principal Designer who added the quest, posted on X/Twitter, saying "I had the honor and privilege of bringing "Kyle's Gone Missing!" into WoW: Forever. Ezra Chatterton was an enormous WoW fan, the creator and voice actor behind Ahab Wheathoof, and the creator of Kyle. A tear was shed during this one, my friends. Rest in peace, Ezra."

The quest isn't hard to get to, especially if you start off as a Tauren. Ezra's NPC is in Bloodhoof Village, which is the first town you get to while questing in Mulgore. You can pick up the quest as soon as you hit level 5, and you'll need to hunt down plainstriders (giant ostrich-looking things) until you get Tender Strider Meat, which you will then feed Kyle to get him to return home.

It's nice to see that while Blizzard has been pretty adamant about keeping the spirit of Classic World of Warcraft alive in Forever, it's willing to add a little wiggle room to add beloved pieces of WoW history like this quest. For as much as World of Warcraft has a reputation for gold selling and general toxicity, it's moments like this that remind me just how magical this game is, and how much it means to so many people.

items.title: System Shock 2 Remaster Is Free to Keep on the Epic Games Store Right Now
items.description: System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster is currently free to claim on the Epic Games Store until October 8, 2026.
items.author: Robert Anderson
items.content:
PC players can currently pick up System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster for free on the Epic Games Store until October 8, 2026. As with all of Epic's weekly freebies, anything you claim during the window stays in your library permanently. You'll need a free Epic Games account to claim System Shock 2, and the game is played through the Epic Games Launcher.

Nightdive Studios, the team behind a string of well-regarded classic revivals such as those for Quake and Star Wars: Dark Forces, released the 25th Anniversary Remaster in June 2025.

The update keeps the original design but modernises how it looks and plays, including the following changes:

  • Remastered visuals, including cutscenes, character models, and weapon models
  • Support for up to 4K at 144fps on PC
  • Adjustable field of view and ultrawide support
  • Full mod support
  • Cross-play co-op for up to four players
  • The choice of an O.S.A., Marine, or Navy background to shape your playstyle

The original System Shock 2 launched back in 1999, developed by Looking Glass Studios and Irrational Games, blending together an FPS shooter with the character building of an RPG. You wake from cryosleep aboard the faster-than-light ship Von Braun in the year 2114 with no memory of who you are, and the ship is overrun by hybrid mutants and hostile robots.

Its influence is hard to overstate. Many of the people behind it went on to make the BioShock games, which are often described as a spiritual successor to System Shock 2, and the game's blend of environmental storytelling and player choice has shaped plenty of what has followed. The original title garnered a 9/10 rating when it received an updated review. Now, this Epic Games Store deal offers a free way to revisit one of the most influential games ever made.

If the remaster whets your appetite, Nightdive also released a full remake of the first System Shock on PC in 2023, rebuilt with new HD visuals, updated controls and a revamped hacking system. It's a handy way to explore the series' roots, though System Shock 2 works perfectly well as a standalone adventure – that's currently $11.99 on Steam with a hefty 70% discount during the Autumn Sale.

Epic is also giving away Buried Stars this week, so it's worth heading to the store for both. It's an anime-style visual novel in which a group of contestants on a TV show must survive a mysterious attack. Like System Shock 2, it's available to claim until 8 October, and you can add both games to your library in a couple of clicks.

items.title: The Miami Heat Will Wear GTA 6-Themed Uniforms in a November Match Against Milwaukee
items.description: The Miami Heat is heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
The Miami Heat is heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks. The one-night-only event, hosted live on ESPN, has been dubbed A Night in Vice City, and will see the home team donning an “all-new uniform on a never-before-seen court.”

Presumably, this means the team is sponsored by Take-Two and Rockstar Games for a GTA 6 marketing stunt. As they go, this is one of the cooler ones.

The event will take place at the Kaseya Center at 7pm EST/ 4pm PT on November 18, the day before GTA launches. A bunch of fancy crossover merch has also appeared on the Miami Heat store, celebrating Vice City.

Yesterday, the top of the Kaseya Center, home of The Heat, was lit up to usher in the collaboration between Rockstar and Miami’s home team. This followed a lengthy negotiation with local officials over the extent to which Rockstar could use Miami as a base for creative advertising.

GTA 6 takes place in Leonida, a fictional recreation of Florida housing its jewel, a virtual recreation of Miami called Vice City. In-game, the Kaseya Center is dubbed the Sahara Arena.

Other studios are taking notice of what Rockstar is doing in the lead-up to launch. Earlier, one of the founders of the studio behind Kingdom Come: Deliverance held up GTA 6’s pricing as a potential turning point for the industry and video game prices in general.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously commented on GTA 6’s price speculation, saying: “Consumers pay for the value that you bring to them, and our job is to charge way way way less of the value delivery.

GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition. The Ultimate Edition, which includes extra in-game content, costs $99.99. GTA 6 releases for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19.

We've got extensive coverage of GTA 6 across IGN. Check out IGN's interview with Rockstar Games, our GTA 6 preview, and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor.

items.title: Batman, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter Feature in First Trailer for Skydance, the Newly Named Parent Company for a Merged Warner Bros. and Paramount
items.description: Once merged, Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones company Warner Bros. will exist alongside Paramount as a sub-brand of Skydance.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Once merged, Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, and Game of Thrones company Warner Bros. will exist alongside Paramount as a sub-brand of Skydance.

The historic film and TV studios are being slapped together by David Ellison and backed by his billionaire dad Larry Ellison in a deal worth $110 billion, following a hostile bid for WB last year and despite various regulatory blocks that have attempted to scupper the deal in the U.S. and abroad. Concern has been raised that the merger may lead to thousands of job losses through corporate consolidation, afford control over a huge chunk of Hollywood to the Ellison family, and in turn risk the independence of news networks such as CNN.

However, opposition to the deal has now largely melted away and, with the merger's completion appearing imminent, Ellison has now confirmed that "Skydance" will be the name of his soon-to-be enormous entertainment empire. The Warner Bros. and Paramount branding will still be kept for their relevant subdivisions.

Indeed, a bombastic new trailer for Skydance has also been revealed, showcasing the vast swath of Warner Bros. and Paramount intellectual property that Skydance will have access to, including the DC Comics, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter franchises.

What once was the peak, is now just the beginning.

Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for… pic.twitter.com/uInLRY3IrE

— David Ellison (@ellisonskydance) October 2, 2026

"These brands are more than a destination, they are the launch pad," a voiceover for the trailer states, in a script that sounds like it was written by an AI. "They don't just live on screens, they move through culture. Each one, distinct. Built on story. Driven by technology. A new center of gravity. A constellation. A shared vision to go beyond. Look up. What once was the peak, is now just the beginning."

Whatever that's supposed to mean, the trailer includes clips from notable WB and Paramount movies and TV series such as Inception, Titanic, Superman, Barbie, Minecraft, The Godfather, The Sopranos, Star Trek, The Matrix, Game of Thrones, The Shawshank Redemption, Casablanca, A Star is Born, Grease, Sinners, Forrest Gump, Dune, Ferris Bueller's Day Off, The Great Gatsby, and Euphoria.

A selection of brand logos shown at the end of the trailer highlights that Skydance will own Paramount, WB, DC Comics, CNN, Paramount+, CBS, Nickelodeon, and HBO Max, plus MTV, TCM, Showtime, Adult Swim, Comedy Central, Cartoon Network, Eurosport, Miramax, NewLine Cinema, Animal Planet, the UK's Channel 5, and many, many more.

The deal that will cement ownership of all this under Skydance is now expected to close on October 6, the companies have said.

items.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance Dev Hopes GTA 6 Will Encourage Studios to Charge More for Their Games
items.description: Warhorse co-founder Martin Klima wants GTA 6 to “blaze a trail” for higher game prices.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Warhorse co-founder Martin Klima wants GTA 6 to “blaze a trail” for higher game prices. Klima claimed triple-A games face an existential problem, with audience sizes plateauing, brick and mortar retail basically dead ("We destroyed retail, and we took all their money,” he said), and no new revenue streams to support the growing costs of making a big game.

Klima claimed that GTA 6 developer Rockstar and parent company Take-Two are in a unique position as the only companies "who can afford, or who can dare, to increase the price of games, which I think is long overdue and also necessary for this business to survive.

"The last thing you can do is to increase the unit price," Klima continued. "That would help a lot, but everybody's scared to death about it. Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost."

These comments come from an interview with PC Gamer, during which Klima admitted that GTA 6 “doesn't appeal to me at all” despite the series’ popularity. "I am not going to be playing GTA 6 unless I'm somehow forced to," he said. "And the reason why it is so popular — it beats me. It's something which I just fail to understand."

In the U.K., GTA 6 is priced £69.99 for the Standard Edition, which is pretty typical for a tentpole triple-A release. However, in the U.S. it’s $79.99 for the Standard Edition, 10 dollars higher than the usual price point of a new game. The Ultimate Edition, which includes in-game content most players will want, costs $99.99.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously commented on GTA 6’s price speculation, saying: “Consumers pay for the value that you bring to them, and our job is to charge way way way less of the value delivery. How you feel about something you buy is the intersection of the thing itself and what you pay for. Consumers need to feel like the thing itself is amazing and the price they were charged was fair for what they got.

“What we think about is making the most spectacular piece of entertainment on Earth, in history — and it’s a pretty daunting challenge. If we do that, and if we’re of service to our customers, then the upside will take care of itself.”

GTA 6 is widely speculated to be the most expensive game ever made, with Take-Two estimated to have spent between $1 billion to $2 billion developing and marketing the title. Yesterday, we wrote a story about a marketing stunt in Miami for GTA 6 that reportedly cost $1 million in itself.

items.title: Ben Affleck Says There's 'Nobody Alive' Who Believes US Politics Is Going Well — And Explains Why He Won't Personally Run for Office
items.description: Former Batman Ben Affleck has revealed the reason he won't run for political office, despite claiming there is a "collective disappointment" in how U.S. politics is currently trending.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Former Batman Ben Affleck has revealed the reason he won't run for political office, despite claiming there is a "collective disappointment" in how U.S. politics is currently trending.

Affleck is soon set to star in Animals, a political thriller for Netflix in which he plays a Los Angeles mayoral candidate involved in the criminal underworld.

Back in the early 2000s, Affleck occasionally expressed interest in following suit (minus the criminal underworld bit), but despite calls from many of his fellow cast members for him to genuinely pursue a political career, Affleck has now spoken out to squash the suggestion and reveal why he has no interest in public office — while simultaneously airing his unhappiness with the current state of the country.

"We don't ask the question of 'what are your qualifications to hold public office?' any longer," Affleck began, talking to Variety. "It's, 'You wanna join the circus? Who's the biggest carny?'

"Whatever side of the aisle you're on, one of the interesting things that people can agree on is a collective disappointment with the way that American politics has trended," the former Batman continued. "There's nobody alive now who thinks, 'hey, we're really doing it right and things are going great and I love this political system.' And that's a problem."

While declining to get into specifics, Affleck stated he could name "lots of things" he believes are wrong with the U.S., as well as fixes for them. Affleck has long been a Democrat party supporter, and has supported every Democratic presidential nominee since Al Gore back in 2000.

"The other thing is where you set up being politician and it's not about serving people, it's just about money, raising money," Affleck added. "It's just about playing a sort of adolescent game of who can make fun of the other person better or be more reductive and stupid about something rather than actually trying to talk about the issues.

"I think the thing that's missing from politics, frankly, is you have to lead. You can't just scare people. You can't just hector them. You can't lecture them. You can't guilt them into it. You've got to inspire them. Otherwise they don't want to vote for you."

So, why not go into politics? Affleck has now responded to say he was happy to stay as an actor, as "selfish" as this may be.

"Selfishly, I just see what a difficult grind of a job it is and I'd rather make movies about it," he concluded.

Earlier this week, Ben Affleck attempted to dismiss concern around Netflix's filmmaking process, in response to past comments from his long-term collaborator Matt Damon. At the same time, he also admitted Animals was riddled with AI elements, following his sale of an AI company to Netflix for around $600 million earlier this year.

Image credit: Michael Buckner/Variety via Getty Images.

items.title: Original Xbox Version of Halo: Combat Evolved Made Available to Play in a Browser
items.description: The original Xbox version of Halo: Combat Evolved has been made available to play in a web browser.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The original Xbox version of Halo: Combat Evolved has been made available to play in a web browser.

This is not a port of Bungie’s seminal 2001 first-person shooter, rather the original Xbox game running in your browser. Hot on the heels of decompilation work done elsewhere, AI developer Mitchell Hynes released Halo in a browser, hosting and maintaining the game himself.

Hynes made a point of explaining that this browser release is not Borderlands developer Gearbox's official and divisive 2003 PC port of Halo: Combat Evolved, no doubt to encourage veteran fans of the original to give it a shot. And his tweets appear to have gathered a great deal of attention. Five hours after releasing the game, it saw nearly 20,000 games, hitting an average of 94 frames per second.

Halo owner Microsoft may well take a dim view of the original Xbox Halo popping up in browsers, of course, despite the fact it’s free to play. Microsoft recently released Halo: Campaign Evolved on PC as well as consoles, and there can be no doubt that the company’s lawyers will see this browser version of the original as competition.

Indeed, some thought Microsoft had already taken action when Hynes’ website was flagged as “Suspected Phishing.” He insisted this was due to an automatic flag from Cloudflare, rather than Microsoft, and the ban was soon lifted.

We’re currently in the middle of an AI video game explosion that has seen various clips of famous games mashed together go viral as people use the likes of Claude to create “mods” much faster than previously possible. Some are using AI to create clones of famous games. Others are using AI to release versions of existing, traditionally made mods — much to their creators’ annoyance.

For video game publishers, the potential impact may be existential. Why buy a new Halo game if AI can spit one out for you in a matter of minutes? This week, the person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda, leading fans to celebrate. It will be interesting to see how long Halo in your browser stays online.

Meanwhile, Microsoft has handed the keys to the next mainline Halo game to Call of Duty company Activision, and gutted Halo Studios in the process.

items.title: 'I've Buried It Deep': X-Men Actor Says He Knew Sony's Spider-Man Spin-Off Kraven Wasn't 'Going Well' During Filming
items.description: Marvel's new X-Men movie star Christopher Abbott has admitted that he knew Sony's Spider-Man spin-off Kraven the Hunter wasn't "going well" while on set.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Marvel's new X-Men movie star Christopher Abbott has admitted that he knew Sony's Spider-Man spin-off Kraven the Hunter wasn't "going well" while on set.

The Girls and Catch-22 actor had a small role in Sony's notoriously-bad Kraven movie, and said it was immediately clear that the film had issues. Speaking via the Happy, Sad, Confused podcast, Abbott recalled not knowing what he was doing on set, and basic details of his character being unclear.

"I can s**t talk myself," Abbott began, saying that he was comfortable critiquing his own performance. "I don't know what I was doing in that thing. I didn't understand what the superpower was, I didn't know what was going on.

"I was like, 'I take off my glasses and what happens?' I feel like no one really had a good answer," he continued. "I don't know what I was wearing in that thing. I've sort of buried it deep down."

Kraven the Hunter was one of Sony's various mediocre Spider-Man Universe spin-offs that the studio pumped out while attempting to establish its own cinematic universe. While the Tom Hardy-starring Venom found success (and gained two sequels of varying quality), Sony also launched the Jared Leto-starring Morbius and Dakota Johnson-starring Madame Web before finally deciding it could not continue.

Various in-development projects were abandoned over the years, including films centered on minor Spider-Man characters such as El Muerto, Jackpot, and Hypno-Hustler. There was also a vague plan to bring these standalone films together via a Sinister Six crossover movie, with groundwork to set this up evident in Morbius' mid-credits scene (which features the MCU's Vulture, played by Michael Keaton) and the post-credits scene of Spider-Man: No Way Home (which features a brief Tom Hardy cameo).

"That was a learning curve," Abbott concluded, reflecting on Kraven the Hunter. "In the moment, I was like... 'I don't think this is going well.'"

"Kraven the Hunter takes aim at the audience and instead shoots itself in the foot with ill-conceived action and a poisonously rote script that totally botches its razor-thin examination of toxic masculinity," we wrote in IGN's Kraven the Hunter review, awarding the film an awful 3/10.

Thankfully, Abbott is being given a fresh crack at the superhero movie genre with a leading role in Jake Schreier's upcoming X-Men reboot. Officially part of the MCU and a key focus for Marvel post-Avengers: Secret Wars, this new version of the X-Men will feature Abbott as Charles Xavier/Professor X, alongside Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Scott Summers/Cyclops and Adam Driver as Nathaniel Milbury /Mr. Sinister. It's a fair bet this will be slightly better than Kraven.

Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP via Getty Images

items.title: With a Smirk, Robert Pattinson Calls Michael Bay's Transformers 'The Definitive Movie of the 2000s'
items.description: On YouTube show The List, presented by movie publisher A24 and Letterboxd, Robert Pattinson and Lance Oppenheim chatted about their favorite movies. During the chat, Pattinson namedropped Michael Bay’s Transformers as “the definitive movie of the 2000s.”
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
On YouTube show The List, presented by movie publisher A24 and Letterboxd, Robert Pattinson and Lance Oppenheim chatted about their favorite movies. During the chat, Pattinson namedropped Michael Bay’s Transformers as “the definitive movie of the 2000s.”

The pair opened up the show talking about movies with bright, saturated colors and glossy tones. According to Pattinson, this style of color grading culminated in Transformers and was never seen again.

Robert Pattinson, of course, is a little scamp. You never know when he’s telling the truth or playing with the audience. Famously, he once lied in an interview about witnessing the death of a clown. As he called out Transformers as the definitive movie of the 2000s, he had the same evil smile on his lips as the clown interview.

Elsewhere in the interview, Pattinson praised Scarface for its balletic action scenes, while Oppenheim said he can tell if he’s going to like someone depending on if they like Tom Cruise movie Vanilla Sky or not.

According to Oppenheim, Pattinson often texts him one word: “Braveheart.” “Think Braveheart.” Pattinson called that movie's famous “you’ll never take our freedom” speech out as one of his favorite movie moments.

The pair were on the show to promote Primetime, a psychological thriller in which Pattinson plays To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. The film’s opening weekend raked in $19.2 million from 2,863 theaters, ranking third in A24’s library, behind Backrooms ($81.4 million) and Civil War ($25.5 million).

IGN's 9/10 Primetime review praises Robert Pattinson for setting "the screen ablaze as a heightened, petulant Chris Hansen." Chris Hansen, the subject of Primetime, called the movie a "fever dream" and has promised to make his own documentary in response.

Pattinson is currently filming The Batman Part 2, which he teased "goes in a completely different direction" to the first movie. Due to the menacing nature of his Primetime character, fans have been asking Pattinson to play The Joker alongside his Batman appearance.

Elsewhere, Pattinson cast doubt on fans hoping to see his dark and gritty take on the Caped Crusader in James Gunn's wider DC universe. "It's such a specific kind of [style], the tone of it gets inside you," he said.

As for Transformers, the Transformers and G.I. Joe crossover movie is now canceled, although Bradley Cooper will star as Duke in a standalone G.I. Joe movie directed by Danny McBride.

Photo by Laurent KOFFEL/Gamma-Rapho via Getty Images.

items.title: Modder Deliberately Corrupts Their Own Hugely Popular Total War: Warhammer III Mod as Row Over AI Escalates
items.description: The creator of one of the most popular Total War: Warhammer III mods ever has deliberately corrupted it so that it will no longer work with “unauthorized reuploads,” amid a row over the rights and wrongs of AI-generated modifications.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The creator of one of the most popular Total War: Warhammer III mods ever has deliberately corrupted it so that it will no longer work with “unauthorized reuploads,” amid a row over the rights and wrongs of AI-generated modifications.

Veteran modder Venris has created Simply Fun Overhaul (SFO) mods for Total War: Warhammer for years, with a popular Patreon helping in the development of the latest version, SFO: Grimhammer III. The mod overhauls the base game to be closer to the lore and Warhammer universe, changing everything from the campaign and battle mechanics to the economy and customization.

Recently, people have used AI to release sub mods of SFO: Grimhammer III that work with updated versions of the main, Creative Assembly-developed video game, without asking permission. In response, Venris corrupted their own mod so that it stops working with these uploads, and threatened to make SFO: Grimhammer III private.

“Due to the growing number of unauthorized reuploads of SFO: Grimhammer III, and more importantly, the use of AI in the process, I have deliberately corrupted the mod to prevent it from functioning with such unauthorized uploads,” Venris said in a statement published online. “If this situation continues to escalate, I will make SFO: Grimhammer III private.

“SFO: Grimhammer is the result of nearly 10 years of passion and love for this community and the fantasy world. As such, I do not permit anyone to take my work without permission. Especially not for AI-related purposes.

“Support modders, not AI.”

Recent weeks have seen an explosion of AI-generated “mods,” which have called into question not just mod creation, but the very foundations of the video game industry. Clips of gameplay showing AI-generated “game-merging mods” have gone viral on social media, with others releasing AI-generated versions of games running on platforms they have yet to be officially released on. Some have used AI to add or expand features, increase player counts, or fuse parts of two different games together.

The mods have raised eyebrows online, and sparked questions about the legality of their release. Some within the traditional modding community have expressed shock and disappointment in AI-generated clones and mashups, and have questioned the continued viability of their hobby.

For video game publishers, the potential impact may be existential. Why buy a new Fallout video game if AI can spit one out for you in a matter of minutes? This week, the person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda, leading fans to celebrate.

But not all oppose AI-generated mods, clones, or video games. “Oh no the horror,” one person said in response to Venris’ post. “Someone forget to get a rubberstamp from a bureaucrat modder whose work depends on the original game devs and publishers anyway. You guys are such losers.”

Most, though, have backed Venris on this. “Anyone that thinks that you are doing something bad here doesn't have experience with someone stealing something that they have spent a major chunk of their life making and it shows,” one person said.

items.title: Disney President Reacts to Live-Action Moana Flop, Says It Was an 'Excellent Film' Hit by 'Unusual Circumstances'
items.description: Disney president Dana Walden has blamed "unusual circumstances" for the live-action Moana movie's disappointing box office, and defended the project as an otherwise "excellent film."
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Disney president Dana Walden has blamed "unusual circumstances" for the live-action Moana movie's disappointing box office, and defended the project as an otherwise "excellent film."

Speaking this week at the Bloomberg Screentime event (via Variety), Walden framed Moana's poor performance as a result of the movie industry being competitive, and the film simply launching at the wrong time.

"It's so competitive right now that you have to have... the right film at the right time, with audiences feeling a certain degree of demand," Walden stated. "I would say our live-action Moana, which is excellent, I think it was hurt by the proximity to our second animated version of Moana, which came together under unusual circumstances, but premiered about 18 months before this one."

The unusual circumstances Walden is referring to here relate to Disney's relatively last-minute pivot that saw Moana 2 change from launching as a Disney+ series to a theatrical movie. This resulted in the project being slotted into Disney's film schedule awkwardly just a year and a half before the long-gestating plans for a live-action film.

"Perhaps there was not enough time to create a lot of pent-up demand for another film," Walden concluded.

While most would agree the timing was indeed awkward, it's fair to point out that this issue is one entirely of Disney's own making. (Perhaps the live-action movie would have performed better if it was held back until a year later, with Moana 2 more of a distant meory?)

But then there's also the matter of the movie's quality. While Walden is unlikely to say anything other than the film being great, the majority of critics disagreed. items.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Filming Delay Reports Spark Concern That Marvel's Multiverse Saga Finale May Be Postponed
items.description: Reports of an Avengers: Secret Wars filming delay have sparked concern among Marvel fans that the movie's release date could be pushed back.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Reports of an Avengers: Secret Wars filming delay have sparked concern among Marvel fans that the movie's release date could be pushed back.

This week, an array of Marvel movie insiders reported hearing that filming on Marvel's big Multiverse Saga finale will now begin later than planned, after previously being set to start last month.

Serial MCU tipsters Daniel Richtman, Alex Perez, and Apocalyptic Horseman appear to have independently verified that Secret Wars shooting will now take place early in 2027, likely in January, sparking concern among fans about the impact this hold up will potentially have.

It's worth making clear that Marvel is yet to give any official update on its production schedule, and it ultimately may not need to do so if there's no impact on Secret Wars' planned December 17, 2027 launch date. That said, the potential of the movie's shooting schedule changing has many fans questioning if the film can still be completed in time.

"Gives the cast time to promote Doomsday during this winter," Marvel fan BTSMGL wrote in one of several lengthy threads on reddit. "I'm not in a rush for Ghost Rider so as long as we get X-Men and BP3 still in 2028, I'm fine with this."

"A *lot* is riding on Doomsday," added vadermaulkylo. "They’re probably waiting to see how it's received before committing to anything. If Doomsday gets a bad critical and/or audience reception then that'll drastically change what they'd do in its second act film."

"I'm getting tired of waiting," concluded own-papaya-4264. "Secret Wars was announced in 2022 for Christs sake."

Principal photography for Avengers: Doomsday lasted five months from April to September 2025, with additional material believed to have been recently shot ahead of the film's December launch. In other words, Marvel has had just over a year to work with the bulk of its footage in post-production.

Just for comparison, Spider-Man: Brand New Day was filmed between August and December 2025, for launch in July 2026. This is a much tighter turnaround of the kind fans now think Secret Wars will need, though Brand New Day is arguably a more straightforward project when compared to Avengers' enormous story scope and sprawling cast list.

Much remains unknown, including the exact date Secret Wars will now begin shooting, and whether Marvel has already banked footage it will incorporate into the movie while previously shooting Doomsday — a tactic used for Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame. Could Secret Wars get delayed? It's possible, though any sense that the film's launch could slip into 2028 would then likely impact the release of Marvel's three subsequent projects already scheduled for that year (X-Men, Ghost Rider, and Black Panther 3).

Still, if a delay is needed to ensure Secret Wars lands as Marvel hopes, a longer wait doesn't seem out of the question. Last month, directors Joe and Anthony Russo teased that Marvel fans need to prepare for "a very surprising ending" to Avengers: Doomsday, which has a "focused propulsive narrative," while still weighing in as one of the studio's longest films to date.

items.title: Person Behind Viral AI-Generated Fallout: New York Game Hauls It Offline, Says Bethesda Issued Cease and Desist
items.description: The person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game has pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
The person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game has pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda.

Earlier this week, a self-styled “AI creative” known as “CHRIS FIRST” on X / Twitter published a video of Fallout: New York, a game built by Claude Opus 5.5 and made playable in a browser. It included quests, companions, dialogue trees, Fallout’s iconic V.A.T.S. combat and even a working Pip-Boy.

Fallout: New York, a full Fallout game you play in your browser, built with Claude Opus 5.5.

Quests. Dialogue trees. V.A.T.S. A working Pip-Boy.

Zero texture files. Zero sound files. Every building, weapon, face and sound is generated by code. pic.twitter.com/58Vls0mOYx

— CHRIS FIRST (@chrisfirst) September 28, 2026

The initial video, viewed 3.5 million times on X / Twitter, sparked a debate about the rights and wrongs of CHRIS FIRST’s use of AI, with some calling the game AI slop, and others impressed by the gameplay. As you’d expect, many responded to the video to predict that Bethesda would eventually step in, although CHRIS FIRST seemed somewhat naive to the situation.

“It’s all free and I make 0 money on it,” he tweeted. “I hope they don’t ask me to take it down. I really love Fallout and this was just a fun tech demo. But I should add a quest where you have to serve someone papers, but they keep running away.”

The inevitable now appears to have happened. CHRIS FIRST published an image of what looks like an official cease and desist from Bethesda parent company, ZeniMax Media Inc, which points to trademark infringement for the use of the 'fallout.nyc' domain name, as well as its use of copyrighted material. IGN has asked Microsoft for comment.

CHRIS FIRST, meanwhile, remained defiant in his post even as he confirmed the removal of the game. “Hey, @BethesdaStudios,” they said, “how about you make a Fallout game instead so I don’t have to? Sorry to everyone who enjoyed the game! But the suits got involved and the fun is over.”

No-one is particularly surprised by Bethesda’s action here. “Dude this game was ass and didn’t even look like Fallout,” one person said. “I don’t know why you tried to cash in on their IP lmao. They had every right to C and D you.”

“How about you make some original game instead of copying existing one?” another person suggested. “Like no one saw this coming from a mile away. Ppl can't expect to rip off an IP and not get dmca'd,” another said. One person commented: “Everything ur AI game did was already done before In Fallout just mixed around. No new mechanics or innovation.”

“Wow it’s almost like stealing is bad,” another said. “Not sure what you expected with your AI trash,” one person declared. "I would genuinely rather play Fallout Tactics than this AI generated garbage," another said. "Everyone liked that," Karl Schecht, aka professional 3D and technical artist and YouTuber Kommander Karl, said.

This week has seen a number of viral clips of AI-generated “game-merging mods” in which Minecraft is fused with other famous games in what is a growing and controversial trend. One such video, which shows Minecraft copied into Elden Ring, was viewed 22 million times on X / Twitter.

I put the entire of game minecraft into elden ring as mod. its runs on Mac. pic.twitter.com/CojefjxtLn

— Anime Girl Worshiper (@TobynJacobs) September 29, 2026

This in turn has sparked a significant debate about the legality around AI-generated clones and these “game-merging mods,” with some wondering if publishers will step in to take action or push for guardrails that prevent their creation within the AI models themselves. One person has released an AI-generated Splatoon clone, which some believe Nintendo will take a look at sooner rather than later. Another person merged Mario with Elden Ring.

so long, gay margit https://t.co/W96dFvpjYI pic.twitter.com/pTTodFIq9v

— Deltaroo Δ (@Deltaroo3D) September 30, 2026

As the debate over AI-generated games rages on, video game publishers will be desperate to keep a tight leash on their franchises. AI is making what was traditionally a painstaking process of reverse-engineering and recompilation significantly faster, which has prompted some to wonder about the future of commercial video game development. Why buy a Switch 2 if you can have AI generate a clone of one of Nintendo's exclusives? Others, though, have pointed out that none of these game-merging mods or clones display any creativity or present any new ideas, rather take existing popular video games and either mash them together or simply replicate what is already playable better elsewhere.

Bethesda is of course working on a number of official Fallout games, including Fallout 5, Fallout 3 and New Vegas remasters, and a spinoff from Fallout: New Vegas developer Obsidian Entertainment. None has a release window, although new Xbox boss Asha Sharma has talked about wanting to double down on the company's biggest franchises, including Fallout.

items.title: Justin Wong and IFC Yipes Literally Commentate Ryu's Match Against Blanka in the Street Fighter Movie
items.description: We already knew about Justin Wong and IFC Yipes’ cameo in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, but it looks like they got to put their commentary skills to work for the part, too.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
We already knew about Justin Wong and IFC Yipes’ cameo in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, but it looks like they got to put their commentary skills to work for the part, too.

Director Kitao Sakurai made sure the fighting game community felt represented in his Street Fighter film, inviting Justin Wong, IFC Yipes, and Maximilian Dood to play criminals in an apparent Shadaloo prison while Blanka (Jason Momoa) and Ryu (Andrew Koji) duke it out for M. Bison’s viewing pleasure.

These three community pillars were shown in a short teaser for the movie back in July. Come October 1, Wong shared some behind-the-scenes footage of his time on set, which included a closer look at the scene he shared with Yipes.

Previously, we only saw the two fighting game pros-turned-commentators going bananas for Blanka and Ryu’s brawl; Wong’s footage shows himself and Yipes literally commentating the match, betting on commissary rations like ramen noodles and toilet paper.

It’s fantastic stuff, and it isn’t the only homage to the competitive scene that's included in the movie. Working with the makeup artists, Wong also gave his character a tattoo of the number 37 — and you can probably guess why he chose that particular ink. (He joked that his character had gotten sent to prison for stabbing someone who kept parrying him, saying, ‘You can’t parry a knife.’)

Speaking of Moment 37, Wong even got recognized by Noah Centineo (Ken), who asked which of the group was responsible for parrying Ken in “that sick-ass fight.” (Wong sheepishly admitted that he was the one who got parried, and later taught Centineo some moves in the game.)

All of the guest influencers got a tour of a few of the film’s sets, which included a look at some of the movie’s props. One of those props appeared to be Mike Haggar’s pipe, which would be an insane reference to include but not totally unexpected, given that Final Fight and Street Fighter take place in the same universe.

Street Fighter hurricane kicks its way into theaters on October 16, 2026. In the meantime, you can check out our interview with David Dastmalchian (M. Bison), who told us all about how he studied real-life dictators to bring Shadaloo’s leader to life.

Image Credits: YouTube/Justin Wong

items.title: Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations Getting New 'Slaughter Mode' as Free Update Next Month
items.description: Doom: The Dark Ages developer id Software has announced a new free update coming to the first-person shooter's Revelations DLC next month: an endless single-player "Slaughter Mode."
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Doom: The Dark Ages developer id Software has announced a new free update coming to the first-person shooter's Revelations DLC next month: an endless single-player "Slaughter Mode."

As announced on today's Slayers Club Live livestream with Doom: The Dark Ages game director Hugo Martin, Slaughter Mode will be "an endless single player mode where players fight through escalating demon waves across multiple arenas, earning cosmetics and their personal best in round/score."

Though id didn't give a specific launch date for the Slaughter Mode update, we can probably rule out November 19! And if you haven't played the stellar The Dark Ages yet, or its excellent expansion, Revelations, now's the time!

Fortunately, id Software carries on after layoffs hit the studio earlier this year, which prompted id co-founders John Romero and John Carmack to each separately comment on the staff reductions, which in turn prompted a response from both the studio and Martin himself.

items.title: Fast & Furious TV Show Greenlit at Peacock, With Vin Diesel as Executive Producer
items.description: The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The Fast & Furious films are getting their own television series, with none other than Vin Diesel himself serving as executive producer.

As reported by Deadline on October 1, 2026, Peacock has officially given the green light for a Fast & Furious show. The series is slated to premier in 2028, the same year that the very last movie in the franchise is also set to release.

Vin Diesel first mentioned the show in May 2026 during a talk at NBCUniversal’s Upfront event, where he explained that fan demand drove Universal Pictures to consider expanding its high-octane IP.

“As you all know, we are very precious about these movies but over the last decade, we’ve realized that the fans have wanted more, they wanted us to expand the legacy characters, their stories,” he said at the event. “And for the last decade, the desire has been for us to enter the TV space.”

Oh and of course, family was part of that decision: “That’s when I knew that the integrity of the characters, the international appeal, what makes us all feel like family will be protected in the TV space,” he added.

Mike Daniels (Sons of Anarchy, PONIES) and Wolfe Coleman (9-1-1: Lone Star) are both writers and co-runners for the show, which is one of four series planned for the Fast & Furious universe. As told by Deadline, one of these shows will be helmed by Nick Wooton (The Endgame) and Charmaine DeGraté (House of the Dragon), while the other two will be handled by Joe Henderson (Lucifer) and Ingrid Escajeda (Griselda).

With this in mind, it doesn’t look like the Fast & Furious world is set to end anytime soon, although its final film is on the horizon. This last movie, titled Fast Forever, is slated to release on March 17, 2028. It will mark the eleventh entry in the film franchise.

Vin Diesel spoke about the movie at Fuel Fest in June, where he detailed how he negotiated with Universal Pictures to bring its last adventure back to Los Angeles.

“The studio said to me, ‘Vin, can we please have the finale of Fast and Furious [in] April 2027?'” he told fans at the event. “I said, ‘Under three conditions.’ First, is to bring the franchise back to L.A.! The second thing was to return to the car culture, to the street racing! The third thing was reuniting Dom and Brian O’Conner.”

Given that O’Conner was played by the late Paul Walker, this statement led fans to wonder how the character will return. Walker’s brother was firmly against the idea of portraying his sibling in in Fast Forever, suggesting that AI could be used to bring him back to the franchise, instead.

With this in mind, it doesn’t look like the Fast & Furious world is set to end anytime soon, although its final film is on the horizon. This last movie, titled Fast Forever, is slated to release on March 17, 2028. It will mark the eleventh entry in the film franchise.

Vin Diesel spoke about the movie at Fuel Fest in June, where he detailed how he negotiated with Universal Pictures to bring its last adventure back to Los Angeles.

“The studio said to me, ‘Vin, can we please have the finale of Fast and Furious [in] April 2027?'” he told fans at the event. “I said, ‘Under three conditions.’ First, is to bring the franchise back to L.A.! The second thing was to return to the car culture, to the street racing! The third thing was reuniting Dom and Brian O’Conner.”

Given that O’Conner was played by the late Paul Walker, this statement led fans to wonder how the character will return. Walker’s brother was firmly against the idea of portraying his sibling in in Fast Forever, suggesting that AI could be used to bring him back to the franchise, instead.

items.title: Viral Short Horror Film Portrait of God Gets Feature-Length Movie Starring Chase Infiniti
items.description: Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature-length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Viral internet short film Portrait of God is getting the Hollywood treatment, with Chase Infiniti set to star in a feature-length adaptation of the YouTube-famous horror video.

If you’re an avid horror fan, chances are you’ve watched Dylan Clark’s viral horror short Portrait of God on YouTube at some point. The seven-and-a-half-minute video centers on college student Mia Reilly as she rehearses a presentation; her topic discusses a mysterious painting — or rather, a photograph of a painting — that, some say, shows a portrait of God.

The photo of said portrait is simply a black image, but testimonies from viewers tell a different story. Reilly says that “some insist they see a person in the darkness,” with subjects claiming in audio recordings that they see a “wrinkled, skinny” man — or at least, something that’s “close to a man.”

I won’t spoil the rest of the short for you, but I highly recommend checking it out if you haven’t seen it yet. Clark packed quite a punch in such a short amount of time, with his video racking up over 10 million views since being uploaded four years ago, and it seems like major studios took notice.

As shared by The Hollywood Reporter, the film has been greenlit by Lionsgate Studios, with Sam Raimi for Ghost House Pictures and Jordan Peele for Monkeypaw set to produce. This is the first time these two have collaborated on a project together.

They aren’t the first to get their hands on Clark’s IP, though; Portrait of God was previously snagged by Universal, but the project fell through in early 2026. Things seem substantially more stable now, given the producers attached, as well as a major actress set to star in the film: Chase Infiniti, who gained wide acclaim for her breakout role in One Battle After Another.

“We’re delighted to deepen our creative partnership with Dylan Clark, whose remarkable talent and distinctive perspective make him one of the most exciting emerging voices in horror,” Lionsgate film’s Adam Fogelson said in a statement. “With Sam and Jordan, two of the genre’s most influential producers, the extraordinary Chase Infiniti starring, and Dylan at the helm, this is an exceptional creative team. We believe they have all the ingredients for a film that is haunting, thought-provoking, and scary as hell.”

“With Blair Witch, I’m experiencing firsthand the trust Lionsgate places in its filmmakers, and I couldn’t be happier that Portrait of God has found a home there, as well,” Clark added. “I’m also thrilled to welcome Chase Infiniti to our team. She blew me away in One Battle After Another and is one of the most exciting young actors working today.”

It’s a big time for indie horror flicks, especially where YouTubers are concerned; Kane Parsons’ Backrooms and Curry Barker’s Obsession were smash hits at the box office, opening the way for adaptations of other popular internet creepypastas like Siren Head (to be produced by Zach Cregger), The Mandela Catalogue, and even The SCP Foundation.

Image Credits: Monica Schipper/Getty Images

items.title: Lanterns Rakes in More Than 18 Million Views Per Episode Globally as Season Finale Approaches
items.description: It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
It’s safe to say that Lanterns is burning bright. The DCU series is raking in millions of views globally, competing with other HBO juggernauts like Euphoria and The Pitt.

As shared by Variety, statistics compiled by media research firm Nielsen show that Lanterns’ seventh episode accrued seven million views within the United States during its first three days, combined across HBO’s cable channels and its streaming service, HBO Max.

In the US, Lanterns is reportedly averaging more than 12 million views per episode; that number increases to 19 million when taking global viewership into account. Variety notes that it’s highly likely these numbers will continue to rise, as 1.5 million new viewers reportedly watched Lanterns’ premier episode just last week.

This is good news for fans of the newly-rebooted DCU, but it’s not surprising; Lanterns has been a big hit with audiences and critics alike, though it’s caused no end of debate among hardcore Lanterns fans, given the fate of one of its central characters. (There’s still hope that this particular person might still be around, though, thanks to some convincing theories making the rounds online.)

With these latest stats in mind, Lanterns is rubbing elbows with other uber-popular HBO releases; DC’s previous series on the streamer, The Penguin, averaged 27 million views per episode back in 2024, while shows like Euphoria averaged 25 million per episode by the end of its third and final season. Award-winning medical drama The Pitt averaged 15.4 million views on Season 2, the finale of which garnered 9.7 million views.

Lanterns is gearing up for its season finale, which airs on HBO Max this coming Sunday, October 4. We have a few burning questions that still need to be answered, and its latest episode has fueled oodles of fan theories, not to mention memes (mostly about Mogo and John Stewart).

IGN’s Jesse Schedeen scored its latest episode an 8 out of 10, praising it for regaining the series lost momentum from episode seven and reconnecting with the “core Hal/John dynamic we love so much."

items.title: New GTA 6 Age Rating Confirms Game Will Feature Sex Scenes
items.description: GTA 6 will have sex scenes, according to a new listing from international ratings boards.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
GTA 6 will have sex scenes, according to a new listing from international ratings boards.

In New Zealand and Australia, GTA 6's store page on PlayStation was updated to include the game's official age rating. A similar thing happened this morning with the UK and American versions of the game, but the New Zealand and Australia versions offer one distinct difference: the mention of sex scenes. Yes, it's true: there will be intercourse in GTA 6.

If you're asking yourself, "Is that different from GTA 5?" Currently, it's a bit unclear. GTA 5's brief rating description on the store page makes no mention of sex scenes, despite there being at least one. Midway through the game, Trevor can be seen getting freaky with Johnny Klebitz's girlfriend (granted, it's pretty brief). Instead, the ratings description just mentions "Sex."

It's unclear if the ratings boards have evolved their language since GTA 5's release nearly a decade and a half ago, or if GTA 6 will feature more scripted, detailed sex scenes more comparable to a film or TV show. It's also possible that the more general, less specific description for GTA 5 is more pointedly referencing the ability to pick up sex workers and engage in intercourse with them. Ratings boards may view these gameplay moments differently from heavily mo-capped sex scenes featured in cutscenes.

GTA 6's sex scenes may be much more focused and graphic, especially since the story revolves around the romantic relationship between Jason and Lucia. Various trailers have shown sensual, intimate scenes between the two characters, so it's possible that the full game will feature some pretty spicy material. Ultimately, all we can do is speculate until we get detailed breakdowns of the specific content that led to this rating, which will surely follow in the coming weeks.

Ultimately, it looks like Rockstar isn't pulling any punches with GTA 6. Rating descriptions have mentioned blood and gore, intense violence, drug use, and more, so it looks like we're in for yet another edgy GTA game. The developer has managed to keep a lot under wraps, but recently revealed that it visited strip clubs in Florida for "research purposes."

We're officially just a month away from GTA 6's release date, so there are sure to be many more marketing beats in the coming weeks. Whether that brings a new trailer or other forms of marketing remains to be seen, but Rockstar has shelled out serious dough for an ad on top of the Miami Heat's arena in Florida and has begun placing ads in New York as of today.

Editor's note: Added clarity and context around GTA 5's original rating and sexual content.
